title: Whither Thee, Da Vinci?
text:
This is a lament for the scholar, artist, genius, mad man or whatever you want to call Da Vinci. I look around and I don’t see many, if any, drawing skulls and painting stoats (well), thinking above AND beyond, wearing cloaks with large beards in Italian heat or writing back to front and upside down.


What would Da Vinci do today? Where would he be? As Trump says: I will tell you: he would be shunted out of society. Left to dwindle on the side-lines as he is ‘too interesting’.


But Da Vinci was a product of his time?! Well we live in boring times.


Now don’t get me started on Diogenes.



— Fin —

title: An Economic Law
text:
If you study economics you get frustrated by the lack of any established laws. Does demand increase supply, do interest rates reduce inflation, does unemployment increase desperation, is anything in equilibrium, do people act in their dog’s self-interest, etc? Mathematics is the economists favourite tool to get no-where with these questions. Anyway I present to you, in this incredible micro-essay, one irrefutable economic law known definitely since the dawn of economics.


“There are a few rich who depend on many more poor.”


Ok this may seem basic but is it not true? And if it is obviously true should not economics be based on this law?


Mull it over and then you will agree with me.


— Fin —
